previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, gastroparesis, and urethral diverticulum was admitted with severe abdominal pain, nausea, and hyperglycemia in the 300s–400s. Initial concerns for diabetic ketoacidosis were addressed with a brief insulin drip, which corrected hyperkalemia and metabolic abnormalities. Her symptoms were attributed to a gastroparesis flare triggered by poor glucose control. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and symptom control, then advanced to a regular diet as her condition improved. A central line was placed for access, and antibiotics were started for a positive urinalysis but later discontinued due to urine culture showing contamination. She stabilized, with normalization of labs and resolution of pain, and was discharged home with increased insulin dosing and scheduled follow-up with primary care and gastroenterology.

# Gastroparesis flare: Resolved with IVF and IV anti-emetics. 
She was able to tolerate PO before being discharged. Case was 
briefly discussed with GI, with several medication changes 
recommended, and outpatient follow-up STRONGLY recommended as 
currently scheduled. She was taken off reglan due to lack of 
efficacy.

# Flank pain: Resolved overnight and recent urine culture was 
unconvincing for infection. Additionally, she had no GU 
symptoms. Given her history of recurrent UTIs causing 
gastroparesis, however, she will be given a 7 day course of 
Bactrim. Urine culture obtained by straight cath had no growth 
(results returned after discharge). Pt contacted to discontinue 
antibiotics.
